topics: Executing, Monitoring, and Controlling a Project

questions.q: Which is an ethical responsibility of a project manager?
o: Taking credit for the team's work
Reporting project status honestly, even when it is behind schedule
Hiding budget overruns from the sponsor
Accepting gifts from vendors for contracts
questions.x: PMI's Code of Ethics emphasizes responsibility, respect, fairness, and honesty.

questions.q: A conflict of interest for a project manager would be:
o: awarding a contract to a company owned by a relative
questions.x: Conflicts of interest must be disclosed and avoided.

questions.q: In Scrum, the person who manages the product backlog and represents the customer is the:
questions.x: The product owner prioritizes the backlog; the Scrum master facilitates the process.

questions.q: The Waterfall approach to project management:
o: completes phases in a fixed sequence, one after another
questions.x: Waterfall is linear: requirements, design, build, test, deploy.

questions.q: Which organization publishes the PMBOK Guide and offers the PMP certification?
questions.x: PMI is the leading professional body for project management.

questions.q: The person responsible for leading a project team and delivering project objectives is the:
questions.x: The project manager plans, executes, and controls the project.

questions.q: Project management is the application of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to:
questions.x: This is the Project Management Institute's definition.

questions.q: Agile project management is characterized by:
o: planning everything once and never changing
short iterations, frequent feedback, and adapting to change
questions.x: Agile delivers work incrementally in sprints.

questions.q: A project is best defined as:
o: a temporary effort with a defined beginning and end to create a unique product, service, or result
a permanent department in a company
questions.x: Projects are temporary and unique; operations are ongoing.

questions.q: The 'triple constraint' of project management refers to:
questions.x: Changing one constraint affects the others and quality.

questions.q: The project sponsor is typically the person who:
o: provides funding and executive support for the project
questions.x: Sponsors champion the project and approve major decisions.

questions.q: The five process groups of project management are:
o: hiring, training, paying, promoting, and firing
initiating, planning, executing, monitoring and controlling, and closing
plan, do, check, act, and repeat
research, design, sell, ship, and bill
questions.x: These process groups describe the project life cycle.

questions.q: The project kickoff meeting is held to:
o: align the team and stakeholders on goals, roles, and plans at the start
questions.x: Kickoffs launch execution with shared understanding.

questions.q: Taking action to reduce the probability or impact of a risk is called:
questions.x: Mitigation lowers risk exposure, e.g., adding extra testing.

questions.q: Prioritizing work with the MoSCoW method sorts requirements into:
o: Must have, Should have, Could have, Won't have
questions.x: MoSCoW helps teams focus on essentials.

questions.q: A deliverable is:
o: a tangible or verifiable product, result, or outcome produced by the project
questions.x: Deliverables are what the project produces.

questions.q: A communications plan defines:
o: who needs what information, when, and how it will be delivered
questions.x: It ensures stakeholders receive timely, appropriate updates.

questions.q: SMART project objectives are:
o: specific, measurable, achievable, relevant, and time-bound
strict, managed, approved, reported, and tracked
simple, modern, accurate, rapid, and tested
small, many, average, random, and timely
questions.x: Clear objectives make success measurable.

questions.q: The project plan (project management plan) is:
o: the approved document describing how the project will be executed, monitored, and closed
questions.x: It integrates scope, schedule, cost, quality, risk, and communication plans.

questions.q: Buying insurance to cover potential losses is which risk response strategy?
questions.x: Transfer shifts the impact of a risk to a third party.

questions.q: Scope creep refers to:
o: uncontrolled growth in project scope without adjusting time, cost, or resources
questions.x: Change control prevents scope creep.

questions.q: Determining stakeholder expectations early helps the project manager:
o: define requirements and avoid conflicts later
questions.x: Understanding needs shapes scope and success criteria.

questions.q: Changing the project plan to eliminate a risk entirely is which response?
questions.x: Avoidance removes the threat, for example by dropping a risky feature.

questions.q: A stakeholder is:
o: anyone who is affected by or can affect the project
questions.x: Stakeholders include sponsors, team members, customers, and community members.

questions.q: A RACI chart identifies who is:
o: Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed for each task
questions.x: A RACI matrix clarifies roles.

questions.q: The critical path is:
o: the longest sequence of dependent tasks, which determines the shortest possible project duration
the shortest path through the project
questions.x: Any delay on the critical path delays the project.

questions.q: A project has tasks A (3 days), B (5 days, after A), and C (4 days, after A). B and C must both finish before D (2 days). What is the project's duration?
questions.x: Critical path A→B→D = 3 + 5 + 2 = 10 days; path A→C→D = 9 days.

questions.q: The document that formally authorizes a project and gives the project manager authority is the:
questions.x: The charter is created during initiation.

questions.q: A stakeholder register is used to:
o: identify stakeholders and record their interests and influence
questions.x: It helps plan stakeholder engagement.

questions.q: The lowest level of a WBS is called a:
questions.x: Work packages can be scheduled, estimated, and assigned.

questions.q: The project scope statement describes:
o: the work and deliverables included in (and excluded from) the project
questions.x: Clear scope prevents misunderstandings.

questions.q: A finish-to-start dependency means:
o: one task must finish before the next can start
two tasks must start at the same time
questions.x: Finish-to-start is the most common dependency type.

questions.q: The scope, schedule, and cost baselines are used to:
o: measure project performance against the approved plan
questions.x: Baselines are reference points for variance analysis.

questions.q: Which software is designed specifically for project scheduling and tracking?
questions.x: Tools like MS Project, Asana, Smartsheet, and Jira manage tasks and timelines.

questions.q: A feasibility study is conducted during project initiation to:
o: determine whether the project is practical and worthwhile
questions.x: It examines technical, financial, and operational viability.

questions.q: Quality control measures in a project are used to:
o: check deliverables to ensure they meet requirements
questions.x: QC includes inspections, testing, and reviews.

questions.q: Using PERT, a task has an optimistic estimate of 4 days, most likely of 6 days, and pessimistic of 14 days. What is the expected duration?
A risk register is a document that:
o: lists identified risks, their probability, impact, owners, and responses
questions.x: The register is updated throughout the project.

questions.q: A Gantt chart displays:
o: project tasks as horizontal bars against a timeline
questions.x: Gantt charts show task start/finish dates and overlaps.

questions.q: The risk management plan describes how the team will:
o: identify, analyze, and respond to project risks
questions.x: Risk planning prepares responses before problems occur.

questions.q: Identifying resources needed for a project includes determining:
questions.x: Resource planning supports realistic estimates.

questions.q: Bottom-up estimating means:
o: letting the customer set all estimates
estimating each work package and adding them up for the total
questions.x: Detailed estimates are usually more accurate.

questions.q: The PERT three-point estimate uses which formula for expected duration?
questions.x: PERT weights the most likely estimate.

questions.q: A milestone in a project schedule is:
o: a significant point or event with zero duration
a task that takes many weeks
questions.x: Milestones mark key achievements, such as 'design approved.'

questions.q: A work breakdown structure (WBS) is:
o: a hierarchical breakdown of project deliverables into smaller, manageable work packages
questions.x: The WBS decomposes scope into work packages.

questions.q: Resource leveling is used to:
o: resolve over-allocation of resources by adjusting the schedule
questions.x: Leveling smooths workloads and may extend the schedule.

questions.q: The difference between quality assurance and quality control is that quality assurance:
o: focuses on improving processes to prevent defects
questions.x: QA is process-focused; QC is product-focused.

questions.q: A project budget estimate that adds extra money for identified risks is called a:
questions.x: Contingency reserves cover 'known unknowns.'

questions.q: Tasks on the critical path have a float (slack) of:
questions.x: Zero float means no delay is possible without delaying the project.

questions.q: Which leadership practice best supports a project team's performance?
questions.x: Clarity and trust help teams perform.

questions.q: A virtual team is a project team whose members:
o: are not part of the project
work from different locations and communicate mainly through technology
questions.x: Virtual teams rely on collaboration tools.

questions.q: Earned value management (EVM) is used to:
o: measure project performance in terms of scope, schedule, and cost
questions.x: EVM compares planned value, earned value, and actual cost.

questions.q: Corrective action in project management is taken to:
o: bring future performance back in line with the plan
questions.x: Corrective action realigns performance with baselines.

questions.q: Tracking project resources includes monitoring:
o: budget spent, materials used, and team availability
questions.x: Resource tracking prevents shortages and overspending.

questions.q: Variance analysis compares:
questions.x: Variances trigger corrective actions.

questions.q: Quality audits during execution help ensure:
o: the sponsor is satisfied with the color scheme
project processes are being followed and are effective
questions.x: Audits are part of quality assurance.

questions.q: The best way for a project manager to resolve conflict between team members is usually to:
o: ignore it until it goes away
remove both members from the team
side with the more senior member automatically
address the issue directly and collaborate on a solution
questions.x: Collaborating (problem solving) addresses root causes.

questions.q: Monitoring and controlling a project includes:
o: tracking performance, comparing it with the plan, and taking corrective action
questions.x: Control keeps the project on track.

questions.q: A status report communicates:
o: progress, issues, and next steps to stakeholders
questions.x: Regular status reporting keeps stakeholders informed.

questions.q: A daily stand-up meeting in Agile is a short meeting in which team members discuss:
o: what they did, what they will do, and any obstacles
questions.x: Stand-ups keep teams coordinated.

questions.q: Tuckman's stages of team development are:
o: forming, storming, norming, performing, and adjourning
questions.x: Teams typically move through these stages.

questions.q: Escalating an issue means:
o: referring it to a higher level of authority for a decision
questions.x: Issues beyond the PM's authority are escalated to the sponsor.

questions.q: An issue log is used to:
o: record and track problems that have occurred and need resolution
questions.x: Issues are current problems; risks are uncertain future events.

questions.q: During which stage of team development do members often experience conflict as they establish roles?
questions.x: Storming is marked by disagreement before norms develop.

questions.q: A dashboard in project management software is used to:
o: display key project metrics visually at a glance
questions.x: Dashboards show schedule, budget, and risk status.

questions.q: When a key task falls behind schedule, the project manager should first:
o: analyze the cause and impact, then take corrective action
questions.x: Corrective action addresses the root cause.

questions.q: Fast tracking a schedule means:
o: performing tasks in parallel that were planned to be done in sequence
questions.x: Fast tracking increases risk of rework.

questions.q: A change control process ensures that:
o: any team member can change scope at any time
changes are reviewed, approved, and documented before being implemented
questions.x: Formal change control prevents scope creep.

questions.q: If a project's schedule performance index (SPI) is 1.2, the project is:
questions.x: SPI = EV ÷ PV; above 1.0 means more work is done than planned.

questions.q: A Kanban board helps teams by:
o: visualizing work in columns such as To Do, In Progress, and Done
questions.x: Kanban limits work in progress and shows flow.

questions.q: Crashing a schedule means:
o: adding resources to critical path tasks to shorten the project duration
closing the project early without approval
questions.x: Crashing usually increases cost.

questions.q: A burndown chart in Agile shows:
o: the amount of work remaining over time
questions.x: The line trends toward zero as work is completed.

questions.q: If a project's cost performance index (CPI) is 0.8, the project is:
questions.x: CPI = EV ÷ AC; below 1.0 means more is being spent than the value earned.

questions.q: Executing a project primarily involves:
o: completing the work defined in the project plan
questions.x: Execution coordinates people and resources to produce deliverables.

questions.q: Motivating project team members can include:
o: recognizing achievements and providing growth opportunities
questions.x: Recognition and meaningful work increase engagement.

questions.q: A cross-functional team includes members from:
o: different departments or areas of expertise
questions.x: Diverse expertise helps solve complex problems.

questions.q: A benefit of documenting lessons learned is that it:
o: helps future project teams avoid repeating mistakes
questions.x: Organizational learning improves future projects.

questions.q: A project's success criteria should be agreed upon:
o: only by the team, not the sponsor
questions.x: Early agreement prevents disputes at closing.

questions.q: Which document confirms that the customer accepts the completed work?
questions.x: Formal sign-off marks acceptance.

questions.q: A post-project review (retrospective) is held to:
o: discuss results and improvements with the team
questions.x: Retrospectives focus on learning.

questions.q: Which is a sign that a project was successful?
o: It went far over budget without approval
It met its objectives within the approved scope, time, and budget
questions.x: Success is defined by the agreed objectives.

questions.q: Releasing team members at closing means:
o: formally ending their project assignments so they can move to other work
asking them to restart the project
questions.x: Resources return to their departments or new projects.

questions.q: Archiving project documents ensures that:
o: no one can see the work again
records are available for future reference, audits, and similar projects
questions.x: Organized archives support organizational knowledge.

questions.q: When closing a project, outstanding issues should be:
o: added to a new project's charter
resolved or formally transferred to an owner
questions.x: Nothing should be left without an owner.

questions.q: Determining whether goals were met is easier when objectives were originally written to be:
questions.x: Measurable objectives provide clear success criteria.

questions.q: Celebrating a milestone or project completion is an example of:
questions.x: Recognition boosts morale.

questions.q: Lessons learned should be gathered:
o: throughout the project and finalized at closing
questions.x: Capturing lessons continuously preserves details.

questions.q: The final phase of a project is:
questions.x: Closing finalizes all activities and formally ends the project.

questions.q: Administrative closure activities include:
o: collecting project records, finalizing documentation, and getting sign-offs
questions.x: Administrative closure formally completes the project.

questions.q: Which activity is part of closing a project?
o: Releasing project resources and archiving records
questions.x: Closing includes contract closeout and documentation.

questions.q: An after-action review typically asks which questions?
o: What was supposed to happen, what happened, why, and what can be improved?
questions.x: AARs are structured learning conversations.

questions.q: A final project report typically summarizes:
o: performance against scope, schedule, cost, and quality goals
questions.x: The report documents outcomes for stakeholders.

questions.q: Measuring stakeholder satisfaction at project closing helps determine:
o: whether the project delivered value from the stakeholders' perspective
questions.x: Satisfaction surveys reveal perceived success.

questions.q: If a project is terminated early, the project manager should still:
o: document the reasons and complete closing procedures
questions.x: Even cancelled projects need proper closure and lessons learned.

questions.q: Transitioning a deliverable to operations means:
o: handing the finished product to the team that will use and maintain it
questions.x: Handover ensures the deliverable is supported after the project.

questions.q: Recognizing team members at the end of a project helps:
o: build morale and encourage future performance
questions.x: Celebrating success rewards effort.

questions.q: Lessons learned documentation captures:
o: what went well and what could be improved for future projects
questions.x: Lessons learned build organizational knowledge.

questions.q: Formal acceptance of project deliverables is obtained from:
questions.x: Sign-off confirms the deliverables meet requirements.

questions.q: Evaluating project results includes comparing outcomes with:
o: the original objectives and success criteria
questions.x: Evaluation determines whether goals were met.

questions.q: Contract closure involves:
o: signing new contracts for the project
confirming all contract terms were met and settling final payments
questions.x: Procurement contracts must be formally closed.
